## Your turn — Exercise 1 {.smaller}

**Exercise 1.** In @sec-gentle-intro you read off OLS fitted values as
`value(X %*% beta)`. Do the classification analogue here: from the (unpenalized) fitted
model, compute the in-sample **predicted probabilities**, turn them into class
predictions at a 0.5 threshold, and report the classification accuracy and a confusion
matrix.

::: {.notes}
**Solution (presenter notes).**

Re-solve the maximum-likelihood fit (the penalized sections above changed `beta`), then
everything is just `value()` of an expression:
```r
psolve(prob)                                  # the unpenalized MLE fit
p_hat <- 1 / (1 + exp(-value(X %*% beta)))    # fitted probabilities
y_hat <- as.numeric(p_hat >= 0.5)             # predicted classes
c(accuracy = mean(y_hat == y))
table(predicted = y_hat, actual = y)
```
The log-odds `X %*% beta` is an *expression*; `value()` evaluates it at the solution,
and the rest is ordinary R. The very same pattern would score *new* data --- just
substitute a new design matrix.
:::

## Your turn — Exercise 2 {.smaller}

**Exercise 2.** Fit a ridge-penalized ($\ell_2$) logistic regression at the same
`lambda = 25` and compare its coefficients with the $\ell_1$ fit above. Which zeroes
coefficients?

::: {.notes}
**Solution (presenter notes).**

```r
l1_fit <- { psolve(Problem(Maximize(loglik - 25 * p_norm(beta, 1))));  value(beta) }
l2_fit <- { psolve(Problem(Maximize(loglik - 25 * sum_squares(beta)))); value(beta) }
data.frame(l1 = round(l1_fit, 3), l2 = round(l2_fit, 3))
```
The $\ell_2$ penalty *shrinks* every coefficient smoothly but zeroes none; the
$\ell_1$ penalty sets several exactly to zero. Same trade-off as ridge vs. lasso in
@sec-elastic-net --- the loss changed, the regularization logic did not.
:::
